keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Sertorian row; the page has no infobox area. Sertorius lands at Baelo in 80 and 'first organized the Lusitanian tribes before returning to the Baetis valley'; the gazetteer's Lusitania region (the Roman province, Portugal south of the Douro and Extremadura) stands for the ground he held in 80-78. Soft edges.

correction.text: Hispania outside the Pyrenean coast and the lower Baetis

keyframe_review.note: From 77 Sertorius holds 'most of the Iberia Peninsula' after 'consolidating both Hispania Ulterior and Citerior between 80 and 77 BC': Tarraconensis, Baetica, Lusitania and Celtiberia without 60-km discs around Tarraco and Cadiz, where Metellus and Pompey hold 'parts of the Baetis line and the Pyrenean coast'. Pompey's eastern campaign of 76-75 and the Ebro fighting of 74-73 are contests inside it; the shape ends with Sertorius' murder in 72 ('normally assumed'; Spann argues 73). Soft edges.

ledger.note: 80 BC: Sertorius 'landed at Baelo in 80 BC' after 'Lusitanian envoys had invited him to lead them'; he 'first organized the Lusitanian tribes before returning to the Baetis valley', presenting himself as proconsul and 'the legitimate Roman governor of Hispania'. A Roman faction state (rule 5: rebel), begun on Lusitanian ground.
